newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan interbank rate ends down, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan interbank rate ends down, seen falling.

text.p: Taiwan's interbank rate reversed its recent uptrend to close lower on Monday, reflecting easing liquidity in the banking system, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate closed at 7.181 percent against Saturday's 7.229 close -- but still far beyond the central bank's 5.00-5.5 percent target zone -- with 30-day commercial paper stabilising at 7.00 against 7.00-7.25.
The maturing of T$36 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit this week would probably flush the market with cash to ease the tight liquidity, dealers said.
They also noted funds that flew out of the banking system earlier this month were gradually returning.
Some bank executives said the central bank has used "moral persuasion" to ask banks to prevent the interbank rate from surging further.
In the bond market, the 86/4 government bond yields rose slightly. Dealers said there was no significant market-moving factors in the bond market at the moment.
